source_papers_profile.paper_title: Drought-induced stress on rainfed and irrigated agriculture: Insights from multi-source satellite-derived ecological indicators
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The paper links exogenous climate forcing to a drought-state index and then to measurable agroecosystem responses, while explicitly testing how irrigation management modifies those responses. Its contribution is primarily explanatory pathway analysis rather than policy instrument design.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Drought in India: Its impact and mitigation strategies – A review
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The manuscript integrates definitions, secondary statistics, and prior studies rather than presenting a single new primary quantitative model; it is explicitly framed as a review of impacts and mitigation strategies.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Combatting groundwater depletion in North-Western India: Obstacles, consequences, and water-saving agronomic approaches
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The manuscript explicitly follows PRISMA, synthesizes prior empirical studies and official statistics rather than generating new primary measurements, and is structured as a thematic review of obstacles, consequences, and interventions.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Groundwater potential mapping in India: A review of approaches and pathways for sustainable management
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The article is explicitly a systematic review with PRISMA flow, consolidating prior Indian GWPZ studies, validation norms and future research directions rather than presenting a single new empirical model or district-level case dataset.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Solving groundwater depletion in India while achieving food security
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The contribution is an optimisation-based policy redesign framework for procurement/irrigation/electricity subsidy interactions rather than a single-biophysical process model; its primary outputs are institutional levers and scenario comparisons aligned with national food security instruments (MSP/PDS).

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Challenges and interventions in water resource management for horticultural crop production in rural and tribal communities in India
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: Single-village empirical inquiry with localized measurements and CropWat scenario outputs; primary contribution is contextual diagnosis and intervention framing rather than a new national-scale causal estimator.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Groundwater Variability in a Semi-Arid River Basin, Central India
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The paper is primarily a hydrological data-analysis and geostatistical remote-sensing integration study (STL trends, kriging, correlation diagnostics) with limited new process-based modelling; it is best classified as technical rather than a narrow econometric mechanism paper.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: The water paradox in India: Managing abundance amid growing scarcity
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The paper is primarily a sector-wide diagnostic and governance review that compiles official/statistical evidence and synthesises policy levers (subsidised electricity, procurement incentives, conservation programmes) rather than estimating a new structural econometric model or a single-site hydrological model from scratch.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Dry and Rainfed Agriculture- Characteristics and Issues to Enhance the Prosperity of Indian Farming Community
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The manuscript does not present new primary data analysis or a single empirical model; it integrates published findings and national programme context to frame dry/rainfed constraints and conservation responses.

source_papers_profile.paper_title: Heavy Rainfall Impact on Agriculture: Crop Risk Assessment with Farmer Participation in the Paravanar Coastal River Basin
source_papers_profile.paper_type_rationale: The paper links measurable rainfall trend and extreme-event frequency to seasonally concentrated agricultural exposure, then traces those signals through expert-weighted impact pathways (waterlogging, erosion, yield loss) to crop-specific risk scores—consistent with mechanism-style assessment rather than a single case calibration of a hydrologic model.

stressor_detection_rules.rule: Flag agricultural water scarcity stress when standardized moisture deficit (moisture_index / SPEI-class) co-occurs with negative soil-moisture or vegetation-stress anomalies and yield suppression versus baseline; use merged per-paper ranges on prec_annual_avg_rain and drought_weeks_trend thresholds where available.

thresholds.prec_annual_avg_rain: use per_paper_ranges envelope (deficit % and mm examples in consolidated_variables)
thresholds.moisture_index: drought-class thresholds where papers cite SPEI or MI classes

stressor_detection_rules.rule: Flag groundwater stress when recharge_rate headroom is low relative to irrigation_demand intensity and g_annual_trend decline / soge_class_name extraction-stage deterioration co-occur; compare merged GW decline rates to consolidated_causal_chains ranges where provided.

thresholds.g_annual_trend: use merged negative trend magnitudes (cm/year) from consolidated_variables

stressor_detection_rules.rule: Flag irrigation-challenge / supply-risk amplification when irrigation_demand or canal/conveyance loss proxies rise while irrigated_area_fraction dependence is high and crop_yield_trend deteriorates without meteorological record drought—suggesting management or infrastructure failure channels.
Flag rainfed risk when rainfed dependence is high and crop_yield_trend is negative with either moisture deficit OR excess-water pathways (waterlogging / heavy-rain frequency) per merged edges.

thresholds.heavy_rainfall_event_frequency: IMD 64.5-115.5 mm day counts where available

evidence_gaps: Single-paper or survey-only links (e.g. some horticulture/tribal irrigation pathways) have confidence low after deduplication.
Cross-stressor bridges from groundwater decline to rainfed crop failure often omit an explicit measured 'irrigation reliability' time series at block scale.
Heavy-rain IMD day counts are basin-specific in one paper and not yet harmonized with all-India gridded extreme-rain products in this batch.
